author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-129724: Intern string constants in the compiler, not per code object (GH-159193)

The compiler merges equal constants of a module through its constant
cache.  intern_constants() then ran on each code object and rebuilt a
frozenset (or, in the free-threaded build, a slice) when one of its
strings was replaced by an already interned one, so a constant shared by
several functions was copied for some of them depending on which strings
happened to be interned in the process.  The class body's __qualname__
constant and co_qualname had the same problem.  marshal then wrote
different bytes for the same source.

Intern the eligible strings of the final constants of each code unit
after optimization and before the code object is created.  Tuples are
updated in place; a frozenset or slice is rebuilt once and stored in the
constant cache so that later units get the same object.  The same code
is used in both builds.

Which strings are interned does not change, except that identifier-like
strings in slice constants are now interned in the default build too.

TestConstantsIdentity compares the identity graph and the marshal
output of code compiled in differently prepared processes, including
names tuples shared with constants.

author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-129724: gh-156504: Make marshal output independent of reference counts (GH-159192)

The marshal writer decided whether an object can be referenced later
(FLAG_REF) from its reference count, so the output for the same value
depended on what else in the process held a reference to its parts, and
differed between the default and the free-threaded builds' view of the
same objects.  This is the remaining cause of gh-129724 and the cause of
gh-156504.

FLAG_REF is now set exactly on the objects which are written more than
once in the dump.  The writer still makes one pass: it records the
position of the type byte of each object it remembers and of each
TYPE_REF, and when the dump is complete it sets the flags and renumbers
the references.  A reference count of one is only used to skip the
hashtable.  Interned strings are no longer flagged unconditionally.

The reader is unchanged and the format version is not bumped: both the
old and the new output are loaded by old and new readers.

PyMarshal_WriteObjectToFile() now builds the data in memory and writes
it with one fwrite(), since the flags are only known at the end.
Nothing is written if the object cannot be marshalled.

author: Christian Aurich Zanettini Martins
message:
gh-159285: Fix crash when copying an empty dict fails with MemoryError (#159286)

copy_lock_held_untracked() asserted that the new empty dict was not
tracked by the GC without checking whether its allocation had failed,
so a debug build dereferenced NULL instead of raising MemoryError. This
affected dict.copy(), PyDict_Copy() and _PyDict_CopyAsDict(), which
type() uses for the class namespace.

author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-155717: Determine multiprocessing's default start method lazily (GH-159254)

gh-155827 made `import multiprocessing` check whether the temporary
directory is writeable in order to choose between "forkserver" and
"spawn" as the default start method. That check ran at import time and
pulled in `multiprocessing.util`, `subprocess`, `tempfile`, `shutil`
and `random`, noticeably slowing down the import for every program,
including ones that never start a process and every spawned child,
the fork server and the resource tracker.

The default start method is now determined the first time it is needed
instead: on the first `get_context()`, `get_start_method()`,
`get_all_start_methods()` or default `Process` start.
`multiprocessing.util` goes back to importing `tempfile` only where it
is used.

Also include the fix from gh-158410 by Vyron Vasileiadis, along with a
test adapted from that PR: when `tempfile` finds no usable temporary
directory at all, the check now reports that instead of raising
`FileNotFoundError`, so that "spawn" is chosen.

The regression was reported, and the lazy approach suggested, by
Leandro Damascena in
https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/155717#issuecomment-6121012448

Co-authored-by: Vyron Vasileiadis <hi@fedonman.com>

message:
gh-62944: Add performance note for out-of-order extraction from compressed archives (GH-151115)

tarfile requires re-decompressing from the beginning of the stream for each
backward seek. Add a note to tarfile.open() documenting this and recommending
in-order extraction or use of TarFile.extractall() for best performance.

author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-159184: Do not compare set elements when marshalling a set (GH-159196)

Set elements are written in the order of their dumps.  They were sorted
as (dump, element) pairs, so elements with the same dump were compared.
That raised TypeError for a set of several complex NaNs, which the
compiler can produce by constant folding, making the module impossible
to marshal.

Sort (dump, index, element) tuples, in which the indexes are all
different.  Elements with the same dump stay in the order of the set,
as float NaNs did before.

author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-159185: Document that PyMarshal_WriteObjectToFile can silently truncate before 3.16 (GH-159201)

gh-159185: Document that the PyMarshal file writers can fail silently before 3.16

In Python 3.15 and earlier, PyMarshal_WriteObjectToFile() ignores most
marshalling errors and all I/O errors: it returns without setting the
error indicator after writing only part of the data.
PyMarshal_WriteLongToFile() ignores I/O errors in the same way.  That
was fixed in 3.16 by gh-155907, which is not backported.  Tell the users
of the older versions so that they can check what was written.

author: Gregory P. Smith
message:
gh-159185: Fix marshalling of a set modified while its elements are marshalled (GH-159195)

Marshalling a set element can run Python code (__buffer__, an audit
hook) which changes the set.  The number of elements was read before
the loop, so a set which grew was written past the end of the list and
one which shrank left NULL items in the list which was then sorted.
Raise RuntimeError("set changed size during iteration") instead.
